```{r}
# Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Read the CSV (adjust path if needed)
df <- read_csv("IHME-GBD_2023_DATA-d3522651-1.csv")

# Filter to the rows we care about
dengue <- df %>%
  filter(metric_name == "Percent",
         age_name == "All ages",
         cause_name == "Dengue")

# ---- Helper: one row per country/year, split by sex ----
extract_sex <- function(sex_label) {
  dengue %>%
    filter(sex_name == sex_label) %>%
    group_by(location_name, year) %>%
    summarise(val = last(val), .groups = "drop") %>%   # dedupe (last wins)
    arrange(location_name, year)
}

adults <- extract_sex("Both")
women  <- extract_sex("Female")
men    <- extract_sex("Male")

# ---- Optional: one row per country, keeping the LATEST year ----
latest_per_country <- function(d) {
  d %>%
    group_by(location_name) %>%
    slice_max(year, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(location_name) %>%
    select(location_name, year, val)
}

adults_latest <- latest_per_country(adults)
women_latest  <- latest_per_country(women)
men_latest    <- latest_per_country(men)

# Dengue val is a proportion (Percent metric). Convert to per 100,000:
dengue_sle <- dengue_sle |>
  mutate(dengue_per100k = val * 100000)

# View results
print(adults_latest)
print(women_latest)
print(men_latest)

# ---- If you want paste-ready R lists (tuples as character vectors) ----
to_list <- function(d) {
  paste0('("', d$location_name, '", ', d$year, ', ', d$val, ')', collapse = ",\n")
}

cat("adults = list(\n", to_list(adults_latest), "\n)\n")
cat("women  = list(\n", to_list(women_latest),  "\n)\n")
cat("men    = list(\n", to_list(men_latest),    "\n)\n")
```
